sentences.text: Well-preserved full body fossils reveal that Paracestracion differed from modern bullhead sharks by possessing a shorter skull and distinct placements for the pelvic girdle and fins.
The genus includes up to six species, such as P. bellis from England and the type species P. falcifer, which is found in both England and Germany.
In contrast, the species P. pectinatus from the Early Cretaceous of France is known only from isolated teeth.
The genus Paracestracion was first described in 1911 by Ernst Hermann Friedrich von Koken in Karl Alfred von Zittel.
Recent studies have classified Paracestracion into its own family, Paracestracionidae.
The parent group of Paracestracion is the family Heterodontidae.
Paracestracion lived from the Early Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous in rocks found in England, France, Germany, and Luxembourg.
This period spans from 184.2 to 132.6 million years ago, covering the Toarcian to the Valanginian stages.
